shipped_promises_as_shipped.unlisted: "Unlisted" is an ACCOUNT-LEVEL DISCOVERY OPT-OUT, not an access control: with users.unlisted true the account's videos and channels are excluded from the public feed, /search/channels and /search/accounts, while the direct video, channel and profile URLs keep serving 200 to anyone — proven live in both directions, anonymously and as B.
shipped_promises_as_shipped.profile_public_default: SEPARATE from unlisted, and privacy-by-default: users.profile_public is BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE (migration 0091) and registration does not opt in, so a brand-new account's profile answers 404 to everyone (and is absent from /search/accounts) until its owner ticks "Make my profile public". Proven on an account that never opted in.
shipped_promises_as_shipped.password_change: THERE IS NO PASSWORD-CHANGE ENDPOINT. Eleven plausible routes were probed as the signed-in owner and every one is 404/405; PATCH /auth/me cannot set a password (the hash is byte-identical after the attempt). The only shipped rotation is the EMAILED RESET: POST /auth/password-reset (always 202, enumeration-safe) -> a single-use expiring token delivered out of band -> POST /auth/password-reset/confirm. Re-verification is therefore by MAILBOX POSSESSION, not by the current password. The only surfaces that re-verify with the current password are deactivate and delete, which are the next slice.
shipped_promises_as_shipped.other_sessions_on_password_change: ResetPassword revokes EVERY session row for the account, so all refresh tokens die at once and every other browser lands signed out on its next load — proven with a second Chromium context that was signed in before the reset and showed "Your session has ended." after a hard reload. But requireAuth verifies the access JWT alone and never re-checks a session row, so an ALREADY-ISSUED access token keeps answering 200 for the rest of its JWT_ACCESS_TTL (default 15 minutes). Proven live: session 2's refresh token was 401 immediately while its access token still returned 200 on GET /auth/me. "Signed out everywhere" is true of refresh tokens instantly and of access tokens within 15 minutes.
shipped_promises_as_shipped.email_change: THERE IS NO EMAIL-CHANGE FLOW AT ALL. Twelve plausible routes were probed and every one is 404/405; PATCH /auth/me rejects an email field with 422 and the stored address is unchanged; PATCH /admin/users/{id} as the instance OWNER also refuses it (422) — the admin surface can only toggle email_verified. An account's address is fixed at registration. What IS shipped is re-verification of the EXISTING address: POST /auth/verify-email -> single-use token -> POST /auth/verify-email/confirm (public, so the link works while logged out), proven end to end twice.
shipped_promises_as_shipped.archive_contents: One JSON attachment named vidra-account-export.json. Top-level sections, all present: vidra_export (version, generated_at, instance), profile, notification_prefs, channels, videos, playlists, comments, follows, saved_videos, watch_history. Field names only: profile{username,display_name,bio,email,email_verified,unlisted,created_at}; channels{id,handle,display_name,description,created_at}; videos{id,title,description,category,language,license,tags,privacy,state,publish_at,channel_handle,original_download_url,created_at,updated_at}; playlists{id,title,description,visibility,video_ids,created_at}; comments{id,video_id,body,created_at,updated_at}; follows{channel_id,channel_handle,followed_at}; saved_videos{video_id,saved_at}; watch_history{video_id,position_seconds,watched_at}; notification_prefs{type,enabled}. WHAT IS MISSING, precisely: media bytes (each video carries an original_download_url instead — documented, v1); the account's own ratings/likes; mutes and blocks; messages; sessions and devices; OAuth/ATProto links; player settings; messaging preferences; search history; donation addresses; and any moderation or audit history. No credential material of any kind — password_hash, bcrypt prefixes, refresh/access tokens, TOTP secrets and the plaintext password are all absent from the downloaded file.
shipped_promises_as_shipped.archive_import: IMPORT IS A SHIPPED CAPABILITY: POST /api/v1/me/import, with a card on /settings. It re-creates only the safe subsets for the CALLER — display name and bio, playlists (items matched by video id, only where the video exists locally), follows of LOCAL channels matched by handle, and known notification-preference types — and reports everything else per section in skipped_sections. Username, email and role are never imported. It is additive: it deletes nothing, follows are idempotent, and re-importing creates duplicate playlists (documented, and reproduced). It is caller-scoped, which cuts both ways: it cannot write another account, but anyone holding A's exported archive can copy A's display name, bio, playlists and follows onto their OWN account.
shipped_promises_as_shipped.export_expiry_and_rerequest: One export may be active per user: a second request while one is pending/running is 409. After completion, requesting again REPLACES the previous archive with a new job id. A finished archive is downloadable until expires_at (user_export_expiration_hours, default 168h, unset in the lab); past it the download is 410 "request a new one" while GET /me/export still answers 200 with download_ready:false, and a fresh request succeeds immediately. Both halves are operator kill-switchable and INDEPENDENT: user_export_enabled off makes POST /me/export 403 feature_disabled while import still works, and vice versa; a normal user cannot touch either switch (403).

SC2_password_change_with_reverification.result: FAIL AS WRITTEN — the criterion's "requires the current password" is not a shipped capability. What IS shipped passes end to end.
SC2_password_change_with_reverification.the_gap: No password-change endpoint exists (11 probes, all 404/405) and none appears on /settings or /settings/security in the browser. A user who knows their password and wants a new one must use the FORGOTTEN-password flow: request a reset link, open their mail, follow it. On an instance with no working SMTP that is not merely inconvenient — it is the only path, so password rotation is impossible.
SC2_password_change_with_reverification.api: 30 assertions, 0 failed. An unknown email still answers 202 and mints no token (enumeration-safe). A's reset: 202, token captured, a WRONG token is 400 with the hash unchanged, a too-short password is 422 with the hash unchanged, the real token is 204 and the hash changes, and a replay of the same token is 400 (single-use). The OLD password is then 401 at login and the NEW one is 200.
SC2_password_change_with_reverification.re_verification_refusal_that_IS_shipped: POST /auth/me/deactivate is the one surface that re-confirms with the current password. Only its REFUSAL path was exercised (deactivation belongs to the next slice and was never completed): a wrong password is 403 "incorrect password" and A stays active; a missing password is 422 and A stays active.
SC2_password_change_with_reverification.other_sessions: See shipped_promises_as_shipped.other_sessions_on_password_change. Every session row predating the reset is revoked; session 2's refresh token is 401 immediately; session 2's already-issued access JWT still answers 200 until its 15-minute TTL runs out. POST /auth/logout-all is the explicit sign-out-everywhere control and answers 204.
SC2_password_change_with_reverification.browser: Driven end to end in Chromium: two live A sessions in separate contexts, then an anonymous third context follows "Forgot your password?" from /login to /reset-password, submits the address, and gets "If an account exists for that email, we've sent a link to reset your password" — the same answer whether or not it exists. /reset-password/confirm?token=… accepts the new password and reports success. BOTH other browser sessions then show "Sign in to manage your account — Your session has ended." after a hard reload, with no settings form rendered. The old password is refused at the login form with "Invalid email/username or password."; the new one signs in and reaches /settings. Screenshots sc2-security-page.png, sc2-reset-done.png, sc2-other-session-signed-out.png and sc2-new-password-in.png were visually inspected.

SC3_email_change_with_reverification.result: FAIL AS WRITTEN — email change is not a shipped capability anywhere in the product. The adjacent shipped flow (verify the existing address) PASSES, including over real SMTP.
SC3_email_change_with_reverification.the_gap: 12 route probes are 404/405; PATCH /auth/me is 422 on an email field; PATCH /admin/users as the instance owner is 422 on one too. An address is fixed at registration and not even an administrator can move it. A user whose email is wrong, or whose mailbox they lose, cannot change it — and because password rotation runs through that same mailbox (SC2), losing it locks the account out of its own password.
SC3_email_change_with_reverification.mail_path_was_exercised_two_ways: This is NOT blocked on the AUTH-03/A05 SMTP-selection gate. (1) The shipped DEV capture seam (DEV_MAIL_CAPTURE_ENABLED, GET /api/v1/dev/email-token, registered only outside production and logged as a loud boot warning) served the reset and verification tokens for the main runs. (2) A REAL SMTP delivery was proven separately against a throwaway Mailpit sink with MAIL_ENABLED=true and the capture seam OFF: 10 assertions, 0 failed — the dev seam was 404, the message was delivered, addressed to the actor and from the configured SMTP_FROM, subject "Confirm your email address on A12 Lab", and the token lifted out of the real message body verified the account (204) with the database agreeing.
SC3_email_change_with_reverification.api: 20 assertions, 0 failed. Verification round trip: unverified -> 202 -> a wrong token is 400 and the account stays unverified -> the mailed token is 204 -> the DB and GET /auth/me both read email_verified true -> a replay is 400 -> re-requesting for an already-verified account is a 202 no-op. B is untouched throughout; an anonymous request is 401. The address itself is the owner's alone: GET /auth/me shows it, the public profile does not carry it, B's read of the admin user list is 403, and the OWNER's is 200 (by design).
SC3_email_change_with_reverification.browser: The verification link was followed in Chromium at /verify-email/confirm?token=…: "Your email has been verified. Thanks!", with an API readback agreeing. /settings shows the address and a "Verify your email" banner with a Resend button, and offers NO control to change it; /settings/security covers 2FA and devices only. Screenshot sc3-verify-email.png was visually inspected.

SC4_account_archive.api: 102 assertions across two drivers, 0 failed. Before any request both /me/export and /me/export/download are 404 and an anonymous request is 401. POST /me/export is 202 pending with download_ready false; a second request while it is in flight is 409; the job completes to done with download_ready true and an expiry stamped; the download is 200 as an attachment. Re-requesting after completion is 202 and produces a NEW job id, replacing the previous archive, and the replacement downloads. Forcing the row past its expiry makes the download 410 while the status still reads 200 with download_ready false, and a fresh request is immediately downloadable again.
SC4_account_archive.wrong_actor: IDOR is structurally impossible rather than merely guarded: /me/export and /me/export/download take NO id parameter, so there is no other user's archive to address; there is no admin route to one either (404). B's calls answer for B — 404 before he has one, and once he requests his own, the download is BOB's archive carrying BOB's email, with A's address appearing nowhere in it. Anonymous is 401.
SC4_account_archive.contents_and_credentials: See shipped_promises_as_shipped.archive_contents. The archive exports STORED notification-preference rows, not effective preferences: an account that never changed one exports an EMPTY notification_prefs list (proven, then proven non-empty after one PATCH). No password_hash, no bcrypt prefix, no refresh/access token, no TOTP secret, and not the plaintext password.
SC4_account_archive.import_round_trip: A's archive imported into a fresh actor: profile_applied true, 1 playlist created with its 1 item matched locally, 1 follow re-created, 1 notification preference applied, and skipped_sections {channels:1, comments:1, saved_videos:1, videos:2, watch_history:1}. Readback: the display name and bio are the archive's, the USERNAME and EMAIL are untouched, the playlist and the follow exist, the preference row is stored disabled — and no channel, comment or video was created. A re-import duplicates the playlist (documented) while the follow stays a single row.
SC4_account_archive.browser: 33 assertions, 0 failed, ZERO 429s. From /settings: the "Your data" card requests an export, POLLS honestly, offers "Download archive" when the job finishes and states the expiry in words; the download is captured as vidra-account-export.json and is Alice's archive with the expected sections and no credential material. B's own card renders his own state. The archive is then imported through the real file input in a fresh actor's context: "Import finished. — Profile: display name and bio applied / Playlists: 1 created, 1 items added / Follows: 1 created / Notification preferences: 1 applied / Not importable from an archive: Channels (1), Comments (1), Saved videos (1), Videos (2), Watch history (1)", with an API readback confirming the new display name and the untouched username and email. Screenshots sc4-export-ready.png and sc4-import-summary.png were visually inspected.

attempts_and_corrections: Six harness bugs were corrected rather than the app. (1) claim-owner answers 201, not 200. (2) The public feed's envelope key is `videos`, not `items`. (3) PATCH /me/notification-prefs takes {"prefs": {...}}, not a bare map. (4) The admin settings route is /admin/instance-settings, not /admin/settings. (5) Three table/column names were guessed wrong against the live schema: comments.user_id (not author_id), channel_follows.follower_id (not user_id). (6) An assertion that a brand-new profile is publicly readable was simply wrong — profile_public defaults to FALSE.

The auth limiter is 10 requests/minute per IP on the auth group, SEPARATE from the general 120/min budget, and a per-process pacer resets between scripts — the run 429'd mid-SC3 and was voided. The pacer is now FILE-BACKED so the shipped limit is respected across every script, and the limit itself was never raised.

The first browser walkthrough tripped the general limiter 7 times (a settings page load costs ~10 API calls). Document loads are now budgeted: a 4s settle after each and a 32s window cool-down every third. Both final walkthroughs recorded ZERO 429s; any 429 voids a run.

The frontend could not reach the API at all on the first browser attempt: CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS defaults to http://localhost:3000, so every call from the lab's 127.0.0.1:3100 origin failed preflight and the sign-in form reported "Couldn't reach the server." The lab now scopes the allow-list to its own origin. Worth keeping: this looks exactly like a broken login.
Access tokens are 15-minute JWTs, so a long lab run silently 401s mid-script. Actor tokens are now re-minted between phases (one login each, paced).

Two walkthroughs failed on state left behind by an ABORTED earlier run (A still private, dave already holding an import). Both now assert from an explicitly established starting state rather than assuming one.
The import summary assertion first read the page's FIRST [role="status"] element, which is a spinner, not the summary; it now scopes to the "Your data" section.

`next start` cannot serve this repo's output:"standalone" build (recorded by the previous slice and re-confirmed): the lab copies .next/static and public into .next/standalone and runs node server.js. The served chunks were checked to come back as application/javascript before the walkthrough ran.
No transcoder runs in this lab, so each fixture video is moved out of 'draft' with a direct UPDATE — a database fixture, not a code change.
unrelated_findings: After a successful import applies the profile, the profile FORM above it still shows the pre-import display name and bio until a reload — the import card never refreshes the session user. Visible in sc4-import-summary.png: the summary reads "display name and bio applied" while the Display name input still reads the old value.

POST /api/v1/me/import accepts a body carrying only the format marker and no profile (200 with an all-zero summary) while the AccountArchive schema lists profile as required. ParseArchive validates the marker and version only. Coherent behaviour, but the schema and the validator disagree about what "a valid archive" is.

The OpenAPI description of PATCH /api/v1/auth/me still says "Partial update of profile fields (display_name, bio)" while the UpdateProfileRequest schema underneath it carries nine more fields including every privacy toggle. The description has drifted; the schema is right.

An account's archive can be imported by anyone who holds the file. It carries no identity, so it cannot write another account — but a leaked archive lets a stranger clone a creator's display name, bio, playlists and follows onto their own account, which is worth an explicit product decision rather than an accident of the design.

GET /api/v1/me/subscriptions returns {"channels": …} while /me/playlists returns {"playlists": …} and /videos returns {"videos": …}; the notification and export endpoints use other shapes again. The envelope key is per-endpoint and cost time in this slice as it did in the last two.

The dev mail-capture seam (DEV_MAIL_CAPTURE_ENABLED) is genuinely well-guarded — refused in production by config validation, logged as a loud boot warning, tokens in memory only, and deliberately absent from the OpenAPI document. It is the reason SC2 and SC3 could be proven without SMTP, and it is worth naming in the runbooks as the supported way to exercise account-security flows on a staging box.
